title: Lior and the Colony
premise: Lena Ravensworth, a xenolinguist whose mind has drifted so far from human speech that she dreams in dead alien tongues, intercepts a distress call in Vessari—a language exterminated two centuries ago along with its speakers. Following the signal to the derelict colony world of Ashfall, she uncovers evidence that the 'Colony Accords' were a cover for genocide, and that the surviving Vessari have hidden themselves by erasing every record of their existence. As Consortium enforcers close in and her own memories begin rewriting in the extinct tongue, Lena must choose between broadcasting the truth—which will doom the survivors—and letting the massacre stay buried. She finds a third path: teaching the hidden Vessari to speak their history through her, so the testimony lives inside witnesses no archive can burn. The book ends with Lena, half-remembering herself as Vessari, standing before a tribunal where the language itself becomes the evidence.
about_author: Isandro Nystrom is the pen name of a former maritime radio operator who spent eleven years relaying messages between ships that rarely answered. They write about distance, translation, and the people who keep talking into silence.

chapters.title: The Long Route
chapters.summary: Lena pilots the relay ship Meridian between silent colony worlds, translating freight manifests and dead frequencies. In her dreams she speaks languages no human taught her. POV: Lena. Beat: loneliness established; her estrangement from human speech feels like grief she can't name.

chapters.title: Signal in a Dead Tongue
chapters.summary: A burst transmission arrives on an obsolete band—in flawless Vessari, a language officially extinct for two hundred years. Lena verifies it three times before believing it. POV: Lena. Beat: wonder curdling into fear; someone is speaking from a grave.

chapters.title: Ashfall
chapters.summary: Lena diverts to the colony world Ashfall, listed in records as a failed agricultural settlement. The landing fields are glassed. Nothing grows, yet something is breathing under the soil. POV: Lena. Beat: dread; the official story begins to crack.

chapters.title: What the Records Say
chapters.summary: In the ruined archive vault, Lena finds immaculate records: the Vessari willingly relocated, peacefully assimilated, gratefully extinct. The documents are too perfect—curated like a crime scene. POV: Lena. Beat: cold anger; the lie has institutional weight.

chapters.title: The Voice Under the Soil
chapters.summary: Following the signal's source, Lena discovers geothermal caves where survivors' descendants live in enforced silence, communicating only in touch and light. A child, Sefi, recognizes Lena's dream-language. POV: Lena. Beat: awe and guilt; she has been dreaming their words for years without knowing why.

chapters.title: Keeper of Names
chapters.summary: Elder Yara-Vesh explains: after the massacre, survivors erased all records to hide, believing memory kept alive invites extermination. But the language is dying anyway—children forget, elders die. POV: Yara-Vesh. Beat: tragic pragmatism; hiding is killing them slowly.

chapters.title: Dreaming Forward
chapters.summary: Lena learns why she dreams Vessari: a dormant neural inheritance—her grandmother was a hidden survivor who never told her. Her fluency isn't learned; it's remembered. POV: Lena. Beat: identity upheaval; she was never fully human in her own mind because she was never only human.

chapters.title: The Consortium Arrives
chapters.summary: A Consortium audit ship enters orbit, ostensibly routine. Its linguistics officer, Dain Corvel, hails Meridian with questions too precise to be accidental. POV: alternating Lena/Corvel. Beat: tightening noose; Corvel is charming, thorough, and hunting exactly this.

chapters.title: Corvel
chapters.summary: Corvel boards under diplomatic pretext. He and Lena spar over tea and translation theory—two people fluent in the same art, serving opposite masters. POV: Corvel. Beat: dangerous attraction; he admires her precisely because she could destroy everything he protects.

chapters.title: The Massacre Tape
chapters.summary: Deep in the caves, Sefi leads Lena to a crystal lattice holding an audio record of the massacre—Vessari voices singing as the fires came. It's proof, but proof in a language no tribunal accepts. POV: Lena. Beat: heartbreak; truth exists but has no legal body.

chapters.title: Love Against Duty
chapters.summary: Lena and Corvel, alone during a storm delay, stop performing. He confesses he suspects the records are false; his duty is to bury suspicion, hers is to unearth it. They almost become allies. POV: both. Beat: tender, doomed intimacy; love arrives at the worst possible moment.

chapters.title: Betrayal or Mercy
chapters.summary: Corvel transmits a partial report to the Consortium—not the caves, but enough to bring investigators. Lena can't tell if he protected the survivors or scheduled their deaths. POV: Lena. Beat: betrayal's ambiguity; trust becomes a translation problem with no dictionary.

chapters.title: Erasure Protocol
chapters.summary: Consortium archives begin purging Vessari references system-wide—the final deletion, triggered by Corvel's report. Within weeks, even the word 'Vessari' will be untranslatable. POV: Corvel. Beat: horror; he realizes what his obedience has unleashed.

chapters.title: The Language Is the Evidence
chapters.summary: Lena proposes the impossible: living testimony. If Vessari speakers stand before a tribunal and speak, the language itself proves the people existed—and that records claiming peaceful extinction are forged. POV: Lena. Beat: desperate hope; the plan requires survivors to unhide.

chapters.title: Yara-Vesh's Refusal
chapters.summary: The elder refuses: exposure means extermination, again. The council votes to seal the caves permanently and let the language die with dignity. POV: Yara-Vesh. Beat: devastating defeat; survival logic and justice logic are irreconcilable.

chapters.title: Sefi Speaks
chapters.summary: Sefi, the child who first recognized Lena, defies the council—she wants to know the sky, not just fear it. Her defection cracks the elders' consensus. POV: Sefi. Beat: defiant hope; the youngest voice breaks two centuries of silence.

chapters.title: The Choice
chapters.summary: Corvel returns, ordered to sterilize Ashfall's cave system as a 'biohazard site.' He gives Lena twelve hours and his access codes—an act of treason. POV: Corvel. Beat: sacrifice; love against duty resolves into duty against institution.

chapters.title: Exodus at Dawn
chapters.summary: Lena evacuates forty-one Vessari to Meridian as Consortium shuttles descend. Yara-Vesh comes last, carrying the massacre lattice. The caves are destroyed behind them. POV: Lena. Beat: breathless escape; grief for the lost home braided with flight toward an uncertain one.

chapters.title: Tribunal
chapters.summary: On the neutral station Verity, Lena forces a hearing by invoking an archaic linguistic-rights clause. Forty-one witnesses take the stand and speak. The courtroom hears a language the archives claim never existed. POV: Lena. Beat: climax; the testimony is undeniable, and so is the danger.

chapters.title: The Verdict That Rewrites
chapters.summary: The tribunal rules the Colony Accords fraudulent. Purged archives must be restored from the survivors' oral memory—Lena becomes the bridge, translating testimony until her own memories blur between tongues. POV: Lena. Beat: triumph at cost; justice requires her to dissolve further into Vessari.

chapters.title: Two Names
chapters.summary: Recovery. Lena dreams now in both languages, whole rather than split. Corvel faces his own tribunal; Sefi teaches the first human children Vessari words. Yara-Vesh plants seeds on a new world. POV: ensemble. Beat: quiet healing; identity as inheritance freely given, not imposed.

chapters.title: The Route Continues
chapters.summary: Meridian flies again, but now the long route carries living voices. Lena broadcasts Vessari lessons on open bands—no longer hiding, no longer alone. The final transmission is a song, and somewhere, someone answers. POV: Lena. Beat: resolution; the worlds that no longer speak begin, at last, to answer.
